Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Sunday is dry and warm under high pressure, but the west-southwest wind at Sierra crest height picks up from early afternoon, so the day favors west-facing sites and turns east- and southeast-facing launches downwind. Thermals are modest: thermal strength (w*) mostly 200 to 250 feet per minute (ft/min), with thermal tops of about 1,800 to 3,000 feet above ground level (AGL). The model matched the light overnight winds at Reno, Stead, Carson City and Minden, and the European model agrees on the crest-level wind, but it shows near-total cloud cover that the National Weather Service (NWS) text does not mention, so thermals could be weaker than shown.

Site Breakdown

Hallelujah Marginal — Wind lines up with launch and gives strong ridge lift from 2pm, but low-level wind shear is at hazardous levels.
Window: 2pm–4:15pm
Before 2pm the wind is light and from the north, which does not suit this west/southwest launch. From 2pm to 4pm it is 10 to 12 mph from 257 to 267 degrees, with ridge lift of +388 to +448 ft/min. Thermals peak at 203 ft/min at 2pm with a 2,590 ft AGL top and fade by 3pm, so the late part is ridge soaring. Wind shear peaks at 7 mph per 100 m at 757 ft AGL, so expect a bumpy band above launch. Land by about 4:15pm for sunset; there is no evening soaring after that.
McClellan Marginal — Light winds and the day's better thermals, but sharp thermals call for experienced pilots.
Window: 12pm–3pm
Thermal strength is 212 to 247 ft/min, with the thermal top rising from 2,004 to 2,847 ft AGL (peak at 1pm) and 122 ft/min left at 3pm. Wind is light (2 to 7 mph) and variable, turning west at 264 to 298 degrees by 2 to 3pm, a cross-wind for this southwest/south launch. Wind shear of 6 mph per 100 m near the thermal top (2,803 ft AGL) means it may be rough topping out. Sharp-thermal caution: the air cools quickly with height (8.1 °C per km), which gives punchy, sharp-edged thermals, so this is for advanced pilots only.
West McClellan Marginal — Wind lines up with launch and there is good ridge lift plus thermals, but a sharp change in wind direction with height needs care.
Window: 12pm–3pm
Wind is 8 to 13 mph from 243 to 259 degrees, matching the west launch, with ridge lift of +186 to +337 ft/min. Thermal strength is 223 to 232 ft/min, with the thermal top rising from 1,831 to 2,656 ft AGL (highest at 2pm), and drops to 76 ft/min by 3pm. Wind direction changes by up to 32 degrees per 100 m, and shear reaches 6 mph per 100 m at 1,891 ft AGL, so expect turbulence climbing out. The air cools at 8.0 °C per km, so thermals will be fairly brisk.
Duck Hill Marginal — The wind only reaches the west edge of the launch range in the early afternoon, and the ridge lift is weak.
Window: 1pm–3pm
The morning wind is from the east-southeast (74 to 151 degrees), which is wrong for this launch. From 1pm to 3pm it turns to 3 to 6 mph from 262 to 275 degrees. Ridge lift peaks at only +131 ft/min, too weak to soar alone, so you will need thermals: 191 to 195 ft/min with a 1,875 to 2,554 ft AGL top. Thermals die after 3pm, so 3pm to 4:15pm is a light-wind sled ride with ridge lift of only +35 to +52 ft/min. Wind shear reaches 6 mph per 100 m at 764 ft AGL.
Daydreams Marginal — Steady ridge lift all day, but thermals are weak and the wind and shear pick up in the afternoon.
Window: 9am–12pm
In the morning the wind is 12 to 15 mph from 232 to 235 degrees, matching the southwest launch, with ridge lift of +216 to +285 ft/min and the crest-level wind at its lightest (10 to 14 knots). Thermal strength is only 101 to 150 ft/min, with tops of about 1,250 to 2,000 ft AGL. From 1pm the wind rises to 18 mph and ridge lift to about +380 ft/min while the crest-level wind strengthens to 26 to 27 knots, so it gets rougher. By 4pm the wind veers to 258 degrees, at the edge of the launch range. Wind shear reaches 6 mph per 100 m at 576 ft AGL.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — Wind blows from the west-southwest all day, which is behind this southeast-facing launch.
Wind is 4 to 15 mph from 213 to 254 degrees, well outside the preferred 104 degrees, and ridge lift is near zero or sinking (down to -67 ft/min at 3pm). Peak thermal strength is 237 ft/min at 1pm with a thermal top of 3,148 ft AGL, but the launch sits in the lee of the Carson Range during the afternoon crest-level wind.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — A strong west-southwest wind of 14 to 24 mph blows over the back of this south/southeast launch all day.
Wind is from 249 to 258 degrees, outside the launch range, with strong sink on the launch face (-527 to -793 ft/min). Thermals are weak and shallow: 215 ft/min peak, 1,410 ft AGL top. Peak 10 m wind is 25 mph.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — Launch wind of 21 to 30 mph is too strong all day.
Wind is from 222 to 244 degrees and strengthens to 30 mph by 4pm (peak 10 m wind 31 mph), with the model showing sink on the launch face (-120 to -170 ft/min). Thermals are the strongest of the sites at 283 ft/min at noon, but the thermal top is only about 1,800 ft AGL and the wind rules it out.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — West to northwest wind all day is a tailwind on this east/northeast-facing ridge.
Wind is 4 to 13 mph from 250 to 341 degrees and ridge lift is zero or negative all day. Thermals reach 237 ft/min at 1pm with a 2,709 ft AGL top, but you cannot launch safely into a tailwind.

Hazards

  • Lee-side rotor and mountain wave: The west-southwest wind at Sierra crest height is 26 to 27 knots from 240 to 252 degrees from 1pm through 6pm (23 knots at 8am, easing to 10 to 14 knots from 9 to 11am). That is enough to drive rotor and gusty sinking winds downwind of the Carson Range and Peavine. NWS Reno also mentions brief low-level wind shear (LLWS) and mountain wave turbulence as winds around 10,000 ft strengthen Sunday, and west-southwest ridgetop winds increasing Sunday afternoon.
  • Strong wind at high launches: Peavine Mountain has 21 to 30 mph and Slide Mountain 14 to 24 mph at launch all day, both from the west-southwest.
  • Low-level wind shear: Hallelujah has shear of 7 mph per 100 m at 757 ft AGL, above the hazard level, and West McClellan's wind direction changes by 32 degrees per 100 m. McClellan, Duck Hill and Daydreams reach 6 mph per 100 m, so expect bumpy layers on climb-out.
  • Sharp thermals: At McClellan (8.1 °C per km) and Rainbow Ridge (8.3 °C per km) the air cools quickly with height, which means punchy, sharp-edged thermals. These are for advanced pilots only.
  • Heavy cloud cover and haze: The model shows average cloud cover of 87 to 100 percent at the sites during flying hours, which could weaken thermals. The NWS discussion does not mention cloud. NWS Reno does mention valley inversions and morning haze that may reduce slant visibility near Reno, and the model does not forecast visibility.
